table_title: List the world's major deserts — those with area of at least 250,000 square kilometres, counting component sub-deserts individually for aggregate regions like the Australian deserts — with each desert's continent, total area in square kilometres, and desert type.
db_analog: SELECT d.desert_name AS desert, d.continent, d.area_sq_km, d.desert_type FROM deserts d WHERE d.area_sq_km >= 250000 AND d.is_aggregate = false ORDER BY d.area_sq_km DESC, d.desert_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of deserts by area' master article + 18 per-desert Wikipedia articles, all accessed 2026-05-12. The universe is 18 named deserts each with area of at least 250,000 square kilometres, as ranked in the master list (the master list's aggregate 'Great Australian Desert' is excluded in favour of its component deserts to avoid double-counting; the master list ranks both the aggregate and the components simultaneously). Continent uses the standard 6-continent classification plus Antarctica (7 distinct values possible; 6 used in staged data). For the multi-continent Arctic Desert, continent is staged as North America under a largest-land-share rule (Canadian Arctic + Greenland account for the largest contiguous land area within the master-list's broader Arctic definition). Area values follow the master list's canonical figure for each desert; some per-desert articles give different area figures (e.g., Arabian master 2.33M vs article 1.86M; Mojave varies between 81K-140K — Mojave is below threshold so not included). Desert Type values use the master list's climate classification, which is the canonical universe-defining source. At this threshold the staged data has 3 distinct values: Polar (2), Subtropical (9), Cold winter (7). The master article's full classification vocabulary is broader than these 3 — it also uses Mild coastal (Atacama 140K, below threshold), Tropical (Ogaden 200K and Danakil 137K, both below threshold), and compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical for some lower-ranked entries; all of these describe deserts below the 250K threshold and do not appear in staged data. All facts are stable physical-geography record.
_extraction_notes: Geographic instance: list the world's largest deserts with continent + area + type. Universe = 18 named deserts with area ≥ 250,000 sq km per Wikipedia's 'List of deserts by area' (after dropping the aggregate Great Australian Desert in favour of its component sub-deserts to avoid double-counting; the master list ranks both the aggregate 1.37M km² and its 6 sub-deserts simultaneously). Threshold of 250,000 sq km picked to (a) yield a clean ~18-row band consistent with recent staged instances and (b) keep the staged Desert Type distribution to the 3 master-list classifications that have multiple representatives at this scale (Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter); the 2 master-list classifications absent from staged data — 'Mild coastal' (Atacama 140K) and 'Tropical' (Ogaden 200K, Danakil 137K) — only appear in deserts below the threshold. Schema: 4 cols (Desert PK + Continent + Area + Desert Type). Continent distribution: Asia 7, North America 5, Africa 2, Oceania 2, Antarctica 1, South America 1 (6 distinct). Desert Type distribution: Polar 2, Subtropical 9, Cold winter 7 (3 distinct). Area range: 264,091 (Thar) - 14,200,000 (Antarctic) sq km. Sort order: Area DESC, Desert ASC. The Arctic Desert entry is multi-continent in the master list (Northern America + Northern Europe + Eastern Europe); staged as North America under a largest-land-share rule. The aggregate-vs-components convention (drop aggregate, keep components) means Great Victoria + Great Sandy are staged individually while the parent Great Australian Desert is omitted. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Desert (common name); (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via master + 18 per-desert articles; (c) explicit relation commitment for the universe (≥ 250,000 sq km per master list, source_defined); (d) deterministic Continent rule for multi-continent edge cases (largest-land-share, with Arctic precedent documented); (e) canonical-source rule for Area (master list wins over per-desert article infobox where they disagree); (f) Desert Type values use a normalized 5-value schema subset {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical} of the master article's broader classification (which also uses compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical for some lower-ranked entries); 3 of the 5 schema values appear in staged data at the ≥250K threshold (Mild coastal and Tropical describe deserts below the threshold).
